title: Inside Newcastle 2.0 - how the project is changing
summary: Matthias Jaissle will take charge of his first friendly as Newcastle United head coach against Valencia as a new era begins.
full_text:
Inside Newcastle 2.0 - how the project is changing
- Published
An era was ending at Newcastle United, but few would have suspected it at the time.
As the team flew home last month, following a 4-1 defeat by Bristol City, Eddie Howe spent the journey watching a chunk of the game back.
Even then, in the final hours of his reign, the head coach who ended Newcastle's long wait for silverware was trying to find answers, to look at what had gone wrong in a seemingly meaningless pre-season friendly at Ashton Gate.
It emerged in public the following morning that a drained Howe had stepped down.
He informed the club's hierarchy of his wish a couple of weeks prior, only to agree to stay on until a successor, Matthias Jaissle, was found.
In truth, though, a new cycle was already beginning on Tyneside.
'We have to build a model here that can compete'
Following a damaging transfer window last summer, and a bruising domestic season, Newcastle have shifted their approach.
They have pivoted towards targeting younger players on the continent, strengthened their data operation and adopted a trading model, which has become especially necessary as part of a restrictive settlement following the club's breach of Uefa's financial rules.
It has not been without pain.
If Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon's departures to Tottenham Hotspur and Barcelona were reluctantly needed to enable Newcastle to truly reinvest, the impending exit of captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal had never been part of the plan.
They have also missed out on top targets such as Spain winger Victor Munoz and Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi, who opted to join Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively.
Newcastle have still made five intriguing signings this summer - goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen, midfielders Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur and forward Bazoumana Toure - but sporting director Ross Wilson knows there is still work to do in the final weeks of the window.
"We have to build a model here that can compete, can win," he said.
"But also one that works for us and doesn't lead us to have to sell players we don't want to sell and lead to Uefa sanctions."
Jaissle's previous experience of developing young players at Red Bull Salzburg will therefore be vital.
There are also some overlaps with his predecessor Howe, which the German discovered in his own research and, likewise, in the analysis the club carried out about him during the interview process.
Yet it has still been a shock to the system.
Newcastle's Premier League opener against Liverpool, on 23 August, was rapidly hurtling down the track by the time the 38-year-old left Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli and was parachuted into the club's pre-season training camp in Spain at the weekend.
Performance director James Bunce likened the situation to a speed dating session because "every moment counts".
That has been evident in Jaissle's first week, which culminates in a friendly against Valencia at the Mestalla on Saturday.
Calm in interviews, but rampaging figure on training pitches
Training always goes up a level when a new manager arrives, as players look to impress, but the intensity of the German's double sessions are said to have been "off the charts".
Such effort is a non-negotiable for Jaissle who, like Howe, wants his players to train the way they play and take that vigour into games.
During his spell at RB Salzburg, where he won back-to-back titles and reached the last 16 of the Champions League, Jaissle's aggressive side ranked first per game in the Austrian league for high turnovers (9.8) and possession won in the final third (5.6) per match.
Al-Ahli posted similarly fierce numbers under him - making 8.2 high turnovers per game and winning 47.6 duels per match - even as he adapted his approach with a new group to win successive Asian Champions League titles.
Striking a balance, as Jaissle did in Saudi Arabia, will be crucial if he is to succeed in the Premier League after he combined front-footed, vertical football with strong defensive foundations.
No wonder Jaissle has already stressed the importance of clean sheets, and the players were left sapped by the sheer number of recovery runs during a particular session.
Training was pared back on Thursday after Jaissle - stopwatch hanging from his neck - recognised the legs of his squad were "heavy".
He cuts a calm individual in interviews, but morphs into a rampaging figure on the training pitches.
Jaissle has brought three assistants with him in Alexander Hauser, Engin Yanova and Florens Koch, two coach analysts in Maximilian Fischer and Steffen Konrad and a goalkeeping coach, Alexander Bade.
But he made it clear how important it was for those already at the club to also "raise the standards" in his opening address.
Knowing Liverpool have had more time to adapt to life under a new manager, Andoni Iraola, staff have been working right up until the early hours on preparation and analysis.
New Czech Republic goalkeeper Hornicek only arrived less than a week ago, for example, but he has been getting a crash course on the added physicality of set-plays in the Premier League and how to cope with towering opposition players attempting to pile in on him following his £25.7m move from Braga.
Is he ready for the fight?
"For sure," Hornicek said.
Newcastle's young side will need such a spirit in the weeks, months and years ahead.

title: Goals galore - the wildest scores in EFL Cup history
summary: BBC Sport looks at some of the wildest games - and scorelines - the EFL Cup has produced as the competition returns for a new season.
full_text:
Goals galore - the wildest scores in EFL Cup history
- Published
The Carabao Cup is back.
Some clubs use the early rounds to give experience to young players, shake off the last of their pre‑season rust and perhaps sneak an early season upset, but that can also result in some staggering scorelines.
From 12‑goal thrillers to 10-0 humiliations and penalty shootouts that threaten to last almost as long as the match itself, the EFL Cup has had it all over the years.
Here's a look at the some of the most wild games the competition has ever produced...
Dagenham & Redbridge 6–6 Brentford (2-4 pens)
Round one, 13 August 2014, Victoria Road
Let's start off with a bang and talk about the joint-highest scoring EFL Cup tie in history.
The tie between Dagenham & Redbridge, then in League Two, and a Brentford side recently promoted to the Championship may not have looked the most interesting on paper, but it certainly delivered a gripping match.
A remarkable match was level at 4-4 after 90 minutes and the goals kept coming in extra-time.
The Daggers took the lead for the first time in the 113th minute and looked set to progress as they led 6-5 late on, before Brentford's Harlee Dean scored in the 117th minute to take the match to penalties.
After Jack Connors and Ashley Chambers missed for Dagenham, skipper Kevin O'Connor stepped up to score the winning spot-kick for Brentford.
Wycombe 3-8 Aston Villa
Round two, 20 September 2005, Adams Park
Aston Villa manager David O'Leary admitted his side were "on the verge" of being part of a cup shock when they faced Wycombe Wanderers in 2005.
But having trailed the League Two side 3-1 at half-time, Villa responded with seven goals in the second half to secure the win.
Some Villa fans reacted angrily when goals from Nathan Tyson, Roger Johnson and Tommy Mooney put Wycombe in a strong position at the halfway stage.
But goals from Milan Baros and James Milner made it 3-3, before a Craig Easton own goal, two from Gareth Barry and further strikes from Milner and Steven Davis completed an emphatic turnaround.
West Ham United 10-0 Bury
Second round, second leg, 25 October 1983, Boleyn Ground
We're going back to the days when the early rounds had two legs, the tournament was called the Milk Cup, and the day West Ham United recorded their record win.
There was little warning that an eye‑catching scoreline was coming, given John Lyall's Division One leaders had only edged the first‑leg tie 2-1 at Fourth Division Bury.
But West Ham raced to a 5-0 half‑time lead, with Alvin Martin, Trevor Brooking and Tony Cottee tearing Bury apart.
Cottee completed his hat‑trick before the break and the Hammers were just as ruthless in the second half.
Cottee added his fourth, Alan Devonshire got another, Ray Stewart buried a penalty, and Brooking tapped in late on as West Ham reached double figures.
Reading 5-7 Arsenal
Fourth round, 30 October 2012, Madejski Stadium
An incredible match, the joint-highest scoring EFL Cup tie in history, and it took extra-time to find a winner.
Still without a win in their return to the Premier League, Reading threw away any joy their fans were feeling as they led Arsenal 4-0 by capitulating to lose 7-5.
Arsenal found themselves four down after 35 minutes, but Theo Walcott's goal before half‑time sparked a comeback that dragged the match into extra-time.
Marouane Chamakh put Arsenal in front for the first time on the night with a goal in the first period of extra-time, only for Reading striker Pavel Pogrebnyak to make it 5-5.
But Walcott restored Arsenal's lead before Chamakh completed the scoring.
A remarkable night was further added to by the faintly ridiculous moment when Olivier Giroud and Francis Coquelin threw their shirts into the crowd, thinking the match was over, only to have to awkwardly ask for them back once they realised extra‑time was still to come.
Manchester City 9-0 Burton Albion
Semi-final first leg, 9 January 2019, Etihad Stadium
Burton Albion's first major semi‑final was somewhat ruined as they were roundly thrashed by Manchester City.
The 3,000 Brewers fans had to battle some M6 chaos just to get there and some might have wished they'd stayed stuck in traffic.
Nigel Clough's side had beaten a mixture of Premier League and Championship sides to get to the last four but were powerless to stop a rampant City side.
Gabriel Jesus scored four, with Kevin de Bruyne, Oleksandr Zinchenko, Phil Foden, Kyle Walker and Riyad Mahrez also scoring against the beleaguered League One side.
After Burton's fairy tale cup run finally ended, Clough said that Pep Guardiola invited him in for a glass of wine and quipped he hoped the Spaniard had "more than a glass."
The second leg finished 1-0 at the Pirelli Stadium, sealing a 10–0 aggregate victory for City.
Liverpool 10-0 Fulham
Second round first leg, 23 September 1986, Anfield
League champions Liverpool showed their class with a 10-goal demolition of Fulham.
Steve McMahon scored four and missed a penalty as the Third Division side were swept aside at Anfield.
Ian Rush and John Wark struck early, Ronnie Whelan added a third, and McMahon scored either side of Wark's second.
He hit the bar from the spot before making it seven, with further goals from Rush, McMahon and Nicol sealing the club's biggest victory in domestic competition.
Liverpool then won the second leg 3-2, advancing 13-2 on aggregate.
Preston North End 1-1 Fulham (16-15 pens)
Third round, 17 September 2024, Deepdale
Yes, 1-1 isn't the most memorable scoreline, but the third-round tie between Preston North End and Fulham in 2024 makes it into the record books after producing the longest penalty shootout in the competition's history.
A total of 34 spot kicks were taken – 31 of which were successfully converted – as Paul Heckingbottom's men booked their place in round four.
Just when it seemed the shootout may never end, Fulham's Timothy Castagne blazed his spot-kick over the bar and Preston midfielder Ryan Ledson – who scored the game's opener in the 36th minute – fired in the decisive penalty.
The shootout eclipsed the previous record set in 2016 when Derby County beat Carlisle United 14-13 on penalties.

title: Liverpool close to signing Barcelona's Araujo on loan
summary: Liverpool are close to signing Uruguay defender Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan from Barcelona, with an option to purchase.
full_text:
Liverpool close to signing Barcelona's Araujo on loan
- Published
Liverpool are close to signing Uruguay defender Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan from Barcelona.
The deal includes an option to buy Araujo, who is expected to link up with the Liverpool squad this weekend.
The 27-year-old centre-back has helped Barca win La Liga in three of the past four seasons, and ended last season as club captain.
Araujo is under contract until 2031 but only made 11 league starts last season, with Gerard Martin and Pau Cubarsi emerging as their preferred central defensive pairing.
After joining Barca from Uruguayan club Boston River in 2018, Araujo has made more than 200 appearances for the Spanish giants.
Liverpool were looking to strengthen their defence after Ibrahima Konate left the Reds to join Real Madrid on a free transfer.

title: Afghanistan’s Rashid takes six wickets in ODI thrashing of Ireland
summary: Rashid Khan forces collapse as Afghanistan beat Ireland by 92 runs in second game of five-match ODI series.
full_text:
Afghanistan’s Rashid takes six wickets in ODI thrashing of Ireland
Rashid Khan forces collapse as Afghanistan beat Ireland by 92 runs in second game of five-match ODI series.
Rashid Khan took six wickets as Afghanistan hammered Ireland by 92 runs in the second one-day international.
Victory saw Afghanistan take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series after the first ODI was washed out.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Argentina and Mexico back Infantino, deepening FIFA divide: What to know
- list 2 of 4Infantino, FIFA try to move beyond botched World Cup sell-off: What we know
- list 3 of 4UEFA’s threatened legal action against Infantino and FIFA: What we know
- list 4 of 4UEFA confirms legal letter served to FIFA after Infantino’s World Cup plan
Ireland lost seven wickets for 63 runs on Friday as they were bowled out for 207 chasing a target of 300 at Bready Cricket Club in the Northern Irish village of Magheramason.
Khan, one of the outstanding leg-spinners of his generation, took four of the last seven wickets to fall as he finished with impressive figures of 6-34 – his third “six for” in ODI cricket. His best bowling in the format remains 7-18 against the West Indies in 2017.
Rashid struck two early blows, firstly having Andy Balbirnie caught behind to end a promising stand of 72 with Cade Carmichael.
Next over, he also had Harry Tector caught behind.
Ireland, in a match reduced by rain to 47 overs per side, needed 156 runs from 137 balls with seven wickets in hand when their collapse truly started with the freak dismissal of Lorcan Tucker.
Mohammed Saleem’s appeal for lbw against Tucker was turned down. But with Tucker attempting a run, Sediqullah Atal, who was at point, ran the batsman out with a direct hit.
Earlier, opener Ibrahim Zadran top-scored with 84 in Afghanistan’s total of 299-8.
The series continues in Belfast on Monday.

title: South Korea FA apologises over ‘sexual services’ allegations
summary: Football association apologises over claims relating to qualifiers for World Cup 2014 and the London 2012 Olympic Games.
full_text:
South Korea FA apologises over ‘sexual services’ allegations
South Korea football association apologises over allegations relating to qualifiers for World Cup 2014 and the London 2012 Olympic Games.
South Korea’s national football association has apologised after a media report alleged it had provided “sexual services” to foreign referees when they were in the country for international matches more than a decade ago.
South Korean broadcaster JTBC reported on Thursday that the Korea Football Association (KFA) had provided such services to foreign referees on multiple occasions in 2011 and 2012, including when they were in the country for qualifying matches for the 2014 World Cup and the 2012 London Olympics.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Argentina and Mexico back Infantino, deepening FIFA divide: What to know
- list 2 of 4Infantino, FIFA try to move beyond botched World Cup sell-off: What we know
- list 3 of 4UEFA’s threatened legal action against Infantino and FIFA: What we know
- list 4 of 4UEFA confirms legal letter served to FIFA after Infantino’s World Cup plan
“We deeply apologise for causing concern over various issues involving the association, which emerged from a parliamentary hearing and an unprecedented search and seizure, and from reports about events from more than a decade ago, that even many within the organisation were unaware of,” the KFA said in a statement on Saturday.
In its news report, JTBC cited a 2016 sports ministry investigation that found the KFA had provided inappropriate entertainment to foreign referees on seven occasions between March 2011 and March 2012, including trips to massage parlours where the fees had included the costs of sexual services.
The KFA did not immediately respond to an email seeking further comment and details.
“The association makes clear that inappropriate conduct of this kind, or the use of corporate cards for such purposes, is absolutely not currently taking place,” the KFA said in its statement.
The allegations add to scrutiny of the association over a separate issue involving the appointment of former national team coach Hong Myung-bo.
Seoul police raided the KFA’s offices on Thursday as part of an investigation related to Hong’s appointment, police told Reuters.
Hong returned as national team coach in 2024 after a previous spell in charge from 2013 to 2014. His appointment drew scrutiny after the KFA abandoned a months-long search involving foreign candidates and selected Hong following a brief meeting.
The controversy resurfaced after South Korea’s disappointing World Cup campaign ended in a group-stage exit.

title: Spanish mountain village braces for astrotourists lured by total solar eclipse
summary:
Somosierra will be prime spot to view celestial alignment on 12 August, an event that poses logistical challenges

Little stirs in the mountains above Somosierra beyond the wind that lashes the flat peaks, the cows that graze on parched grass and the sun that beats down on the abandoned aerodrome where generations of glider pilots learned to ride air currents alongside squadrons of vultures and red kites.

But all this stillness will disappear, albeit temporarily, on the evening of 12 August, when swathes of northern and eastern Spain and the Balearic islands experience a total solar eclipse, the likes of which has not been seen here for more than 120 years.

full_text:
Little stirs in the mountains above Somosierra beyond the wind that lashes the flat peaks, the cows that graze on parched grass and the sun that beats down on the abandoned aerodrome where generations of glider pilots learned to ride air currents alongside squadrons of vultures and red kites.
But all this stillness will disappear, albeit temporarily, on the evening of 12 August, when swathes of northern and eastern Spain and the Balearic islands experience a total solar eclipse, the likes of which has not been seen here for more than 120 years.
The rare celestial alignment has suddenly turned Somosierra – a small village that sits at an altitude of 1,440 metres where the northernmost reaches of the Madrid region fade into neighbouring Castilla y León and Castilla-La Mancha – into a prime astrotourist destination. No site as close to the Spanish capital will enjoy what Somosierra will: one minute and 29 seconds of pure, clear-skied total eclipse.
Awe-inspiring as the event promises to be, however, it has thrown up all sorts of unexpected but pressing questions for the village and its 93 inhabitants.
With as many as 2,000 visitors expected, where will everyone park? Will there be enough water? And, last but not least, how many batches of paella will the local restaurant need to prepare for the invasion of hungry sky-gazers?
“The fact that we’ve been selected as the best place in the Madrid region to watch the eclipse has led to a huge amount of media and social media coverage,” said Somosierra council’s tourism manager, Irma López Muñoz, as she looked out across the eclipse observation site, a 10-minute drive up past the village.
“That’s generated a lot of interest among people in Madrid – and some from abroad. So we’re anticipating a large influx of visitors because it is a unique event that hasn’t been seen for over 100 years.”
Even before the recent massive wildfires broke out to the west of Madrid, Somosierra council was thinking about how to minimise risk factors on the day of the eclipse and has been coordinating its efforts with police and civil protection authorities.
Although the village council has offered 400 official registration slots, it believes five times as many people could turn up on the day.
“We’re very close to a major European capital with a huge population, and many people are going to come without seeking out information beforehand,” added López. “That’s beyond our control. We can’t predict that someone might be watching television and say, ‘Well, I’m going to make some sandwiches and go see the eclipse with my children.’”
With that in mind, the council is scrambling to recruit and educate volunteers to help steward events on 12 August. It recently hired El Nocturnario, a company of astrotourism experts, to deliver a day’s training to the volunteers who had gathered in Somosierra’s tiny cultural centre to learn about the joys and dangers of eclipses.
One of the volunteers, María Gradaille, said she was delighted to help out with what she called “a once-in-a-lifetime event and a historic scientific milestone”. She was also grateful for the knowledge and the tips she had picked up at the training session.
“I’ve learned so much about the eclipse,” she said. “I didn’t know it could burn your eyes so badly or just how dangerous it can be.”
According to Sarai de la Hoz, one of El Nocturnario’s co-founders, local and regional authorities around Spain are belatedly beginning to wake up the potential benefits of all things astronomical. The looming total solar eclipse will be followed by a six-minute-long “eclipse of the century” in August next year, and by a spectacular “ring of fire eclipse” in January 2028.
Little wonder, then, that the Spanish government has set up a special committee to oversee the trio of eclipses. As the government spokesperson Elma Saiz Delgado pointed out on Tuesday, the events will put Spain “at the centre of global astronomical observation and astrotourism”. This first eclipse alone is expected to attract 446,000 additional visitors in a year when tourist numbers in Spain could pass the 100-million mark for the first time. The event is also forecast to bring in an extra €342m (£292m) in tourist revenue.
“When we started talking about the eclipse a year ago, people kind of thought we were mad. They were like: ‘It’s not going to be that big a deal’ and: ‘Not that many people will come,’” said De la Hoz, “But as time’s gone by and the authorities have realised what’s to come, we’re been getting calls from people who need our help.”
While much of the training she and her colleagues provide is about eclipses and how to watch one safely, the classes also involve a lot of logistics and organisation: “How’s the event going to be organised; who’s going to liaise with the local police and the civil protection authorities, and how will you deal with parking and people at the venue?”
Authorities in the Balearics, which are bracing for huge numbers of extra visitors, have already announced that restrictions will be introduced on 20 main roads across Mallorca, Ibiza, Menorca and Formentera from 3pm until 9pm on the day of the eclipse to prevent gridlock.
Practicalities of a rather different nature are on the mind of Yolanda Cerezo, who has run the Hotel Restaurante El Puerto de Somosierra for the past 26 years. Sitting on the shady terrace of the hotel and restaurant, Cerezo pondered the possibility of a tenfold increase in the 200 to 300 customers she would normally serve on a busy day.
“We’ve had some big one-day events and parties, but we’ve never seen this kind of volume,” she said. “The eclipse is going to be a long day, but we have to make the most of it. We’re not going to see another day like it, are we? It’ll be unique.”
Cerezo, who also caters events, is hoping to get the necessary licences to set up a stall and a bar at the observation site. If she succeeds, she will need to hire another eight or nine people to supplement the restaurant’s regular workforce of nine people. Menu-wise, she’s thinking lamb stew, paella and an assortment of hot and cold sandwiches, all of which can be prepared in the hotel kitchen and driven up the mountain.
“If I do a massive paella and it runs out, I’ll ring down to my people in the kitchen here and they’ll prepare another one and bring it up,” she said. “We can’t leave people stuck halfway up a mountain with nothing to eat.”

title: U.S. Senate opens first stage of crypto Clarity Act voting to give bill a chance next month
full_text:
U.S. Senate opens first stage of crypto Clarity Act voting to give bill a chance next month
The majority leader opened the multi-stage process the Senate follows when trying to get a bill over its 60-vote hurdle, so it's still got a shot in September.
- Senate Majority Leader filed the motion to proceed on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act early Saturday, after a marathon overnight Senate voting session.
- While the motion came too late for the Senate to vote on the crypto market structure bill before the body breaks for its August recess, the move sets the bill up for an initial vote almost immediately after the Senate returns next month.
- There are a number of outstanding issues lawmakers need to come to agreements on for a successful vote, including government ethics, law enforcement provisions and stablecoin yield and rewards.
The U.S. Senate is finally leaping into the first procedural votes on the crypto Digital Assets Market Clarity Act, after the leadership moved early Saturday to start official floor action on the crypto market structure bill, marking the farthest progress yet for the industry's central policy effort.
But this key advance announced after a marathon overnight voting session comes after the bill has missed its window to get a vote before the Senate's summer break, leaving it in a long-shot position to get approval in September. Though the Clarity Act's chances are hanging by a thread, it would likely have been declared dead for 2026 without at least this first important movement.
"We, the undersigned senators … hereby move to bring to a close debate on the motion to proceed to calendar number 423, [House Resolution] 3633, an act to provide for a system of regulation of the offer and sale of digital commodities by the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and so forth and for other purposes," the clerk said reading the filing.
The legislation now gets into a crowded line to move through an arcane Senate procedure known as cloture, which involves a number of steps and waiting periods before a disputed piece of legislation can reach a final vote. Clarity joins a number of other unfinished bills heading toward a three-week window of Senate floor time in September — the final period before Congress leaves Washington and lawmakers devote their attention to the November midterm elections. Still, Majority Leader John Thune's move to begin this process means the Senate can get to its first procedural vote almost immediately after it returns, potentially clearing that initial hurdle on day two of the September session.
The negotiators have several weeks to come up with answers for a number of disagreements still hanging over the bill, including the details of its illicit-finance protections, the lingering dispute over stablecoin rewards and its government-ethics provision.
Clarity is likely to require the support of at least 10 Senate Democrats if it's going to clear the 60-vote threshold needed to pass Senate bills. So far, that support has been in doubt as the Democrats who have been most involved in trying to advance the legislation have dug in their heels over Clarity's ban against senior government officials, including President Donald Trump, backing crypto projects.
A revised proposal on that section, written by a bipartisan pair of senators, has sat unanswered for at least a week at the White House. Trump would probably need to sign off before the Clarity Act could move forward as a bipartisan bill.
But negotiations continue on that and other points, and industry insiders are still hoping they can bridge the gaps and fulfill their top goal for 2026. Senate and industry staffers both told CoinDesk on Friday, after Thune confirmed there wouldn't be a vote on Clarity in August, that the September timeline was doable should lawmakers come to an agreement on these issues. From a strict timeline perspective, Senators only need a handful of days across the three weeks they'll be in session next month to get through the voting process.
Senate Majority Leader Thune warned weeks ago that he doubted the bill would get a final vote before the August break, and he had signaled that other Senate work needed more urgent attention, such as bills on federal funding, Russia sanctions and nominations, which the Senate powered through on Friday night. So this last-minute pursuit of the Clarity Act could be marked as a positive sign of optimism from his office.
So what exactly happened on Saturday morning? Thune pursued a formal motion to proceed on this legislation to establish a regulatory regime for the U.S. crypto markets. The process is used for setting up debate on a bill that's set for floor voting but doesn't have a shot at unanimous approval.
Cloture requires 60 yes votes to move forward. Clarity's first test could go one of two ways: The negotiations lead to a sudden pre-vote agreement that convinces a lot of Democrats to get on board, in which case the bill could keep steaming toward a final vote. Or, the procedural vote becomes a political exercise to force resistant lawmakers to make their oppositions official, in which case Clarity becomes a campaign battleground in which crypto political action committees, such as Fairshake, can make spending decisions based on politicians' votes.
If the partisan rift remains when the senators vote, it's highly unlikely that Clarity can become law this year. And next year will start a new Congress — potentially with Democrats controlling the agenda in at least one of the chambers — which would probably require the industry to reset and start anew.

title: Hairmax LaserBand 82 ComfortFlex Review: Putting Down New Roots
summary: Hairmax’s LaserBand 82 ComfortFlex took only 90 seconds per treatment, and it produced visible results along my widening part.
full_text:
I’ve had long, thick hair for most of my life. Right up until my early forties, in fact, when large handfuls of my hair started falling out in the shower. “Why is this happening?” I asked my doctor at the time, as my front part began widening at an alarming rate.
My doctor ran thyroid tests, iron-deficiency tests, and pretty much every other test except for the estrogen and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) labs that, a couple years later, would ultimately indicate the problem: perimenopause. Fluctuating estrogen and progesterone hormones in the years right before menopause often cause a dominance of androgens, or male hormones like testosterone and androstenedione. In genetically susceptible women (like me, apparently), such androgens can shrink hair follicles and cause pattern baldness.
This was new information to me. I knew older women often wore their hair in a short, fluffy bouffant, but until I started shedding, I thought it was a style thing, not a strategy to cover their balding heads. I knew I was now in a race against time, so the concept of red-light devices for hair growth caught my attention—specifically, the quick-treatment Hairmax LaserBand, which only takes 30 seconds for each area of your head. (I do three sessions to cover my scalp.) As a full-time working parent, my daily mental load already defies the laws of physics; if a beauty regimen takes longer than a minute or two, I’m probably just not going to do it.
I’ve now been using the Hairmax for five months, and while the results didn’t exactly constitute a miracle, they were definitely noticeable.
Laser-Sharp
Clinical trials have shown that red-light therapy can help increase blood circulation and reduce inflammation, which can lead to increased collagen production in the skin. It’s not a huge leap to see how this benefit could extend to hair follicles in the scalp. In fact, studies show that red light can energize hair follicles and lower levels of dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which is another androgen that can cause hair loss.
Red light can also support the production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), an energy-carrying molecule that helps existing follicles remain in the hair-growth phase. However, while these devices can promote a healthy environment for living hair follicles, they can’t revive follicles that are scarred or long dormant. If parts of your scalp are totally bald and shiny, you may need to go to Turkey after all.
The Hairmax LaserBand, a 3-inch-thick blue headband with teeth, looks a lot like a shark mouth when sitting on its charging cradle, which is both a handy resting place and keeps it charged at all times. It's pricey—a few hundred more than similar devices. But unlike a lot of competitors, like CurrentBody’s LED helmet and HigherDose’s ball cap-style hat, the LaserBand contains no LEDs in favor of more targeted red-light laser diodes. (Some competitors, like GroWell and iRestore, use a mix of LEDs and laser diodes.)

title: Spokane Shows What the New Era of Wildfires Looks Like
summary: With rising temperatures and drier conditions, fires are more likely to explode. And with more people living next to forests, the results can be catastrophic.
full_text:
Betsy Robertson was standing in the center of the Spokane Convention Center on Monday afternoon, but she wasn’t there for a gala or a conference. Instead, the event space in the middle of Washington state’s second-largest city had been transformed into a Red Cross emergency shelter as a trio of wildfires, just a few miles away, burned down entire neighborhoods.
Nurses and volunteers were moving between the rows of cots around Robertson, making sure that the hundreds of evacuees—from the mothers with their babies to the elderly with their caretakers—had blankets and enough to eat. Just outside, the air was noxious with smoke “thick enough to burn your eyes,” she said.
Robertson, a communications director for the Red Cross, is from Washington and has been with the organization for 10 years. She has seen communities devastated by wildfires before. But never like this.
“The scale of homes destroyed and lives changed forever—this is a new level,” she said. “We are bracing ourselves for seasons like this getting worse and worse, and starting earlier and going later.”
A historically dry winter, extreme drought, and heat waves set the stage for the hundreds of wildfires that have burned across the Pacific Northwest this summer. Dozens of large ones have broken out in the past week alone. Though it’s still early in the fire season, Oregon recently broke its annual record for acreage burned with nearly 2 million acres scorched.
Washington is also in the middle of its most destructive season on record, with more than half a million acres burned and at least 65,000 residents ordered to evacuate across the state. The three large fires that started on Saturday around Spokane had destroyed more than 700 buildings by Monday afternoon.
“I’ve been trying to wrap my mind around how we’re going to house all these folks,” said Kitty Klitzke, a member of the Spokane City Council representing a hard-hit area where two fires were burning on Tuesday morning. Many of the people displaced by the fires in Spokane are senior citizens and their caretakers. “It’s a miracle that, so far, we know of no fatalities and no reported missing people,” Klitzke said.
As the planet heats up, the conditions that fuel extreme wildfires are becoming more common. A warmer atmosphere can hold about 7 percent more water vapor for every 1 degree Celsius of warming, drawing more moisture from soils and vegetation and leaving forests and grasslands primed to burn. That dynamic also causes rain to fall more intensely but less frequently, leading to long periods of drought.
“This fire, and what we’re expecting to come, makes no sense unless you connect the dots through a changing climate,” said Bob Freitag, who recently served as director of the Institute of Hazards Mitigation Research and Planning at the University of Washington. “The science is known, and this is not something that is a one-off.”
According to Paul Pastelok, a senior meteorologist at AccuWeather, a lack of snowfall across the region helped set the stage for these fires. Normally, snowpack builds up during the winter and melts gradually through the rest of the year, providing a steady source of moisture. This year, the already-small snowpack was hit with hot spring temperatures, causing this reserve to melt early and leaving the landscape parched. Spokane had half of the typical snowfall this year, Pastelok said. Other parts of the state had even less, with many areas reaching historic lows.
In the past few days, powerful winds carried hot embers from the Little Giant fire, a 70,000-acre blaze in central Washington, for more than 3 miles, sending the flames clear over the waters of Lake Chelan and into the forests on the other side. Ryan Rodruck, a communications manager at the Washington Department of Natural Resources, called the overall situation “extremely tragic” and said that it had been an exceptionally challenging season for the thousands of wildland firefighters deployed across the state.
In Spokane, more high winds forecast for this weekend could further worsen conditions, said Benjamin Cossel, a wildfire public information officer from California working with firefighting crews in the city.
The situation is comparable to the Los Angeles fires in 2025, Cossel said. Both outbreaks began in wild areas before moving into partially forested suburban neighborhoods. The urban setting also makes the smoke especially toxic, he said. A recently released study found that the Los Angeles fires, which sent more than 200,000 residents fleeing, had exposed an estimated 3.3 million people to high concentrations of a cancer-causing toxin.
Klitzke, the city council member, said the affected neighborhoods in Spokane were known to be vulnerable to fires. Steep terrain and abundant plant life helped the fires spread quickly over the weekend, while the winding cul-de-sac layouts of the neighborhoods slowed evacuations and made it difficult for emergency responders to reach the fires.
“These are neighborhoods with thousands of people and only two ways in or out,” Klitzke said, adding that many evacuees were stuck waiting in traffic for hours, watching the houses around them burn down.
Areas where homes mingle with natural areas are known as the wildland-urban interface. This kind of suburban housing is the fastest growing type of land development in the United States, and research shows that the homes built in these areas are more likely to burn down when wildfires spread.
“We already knew that this was a dangerous situation,” she said. “We need to get really serious about addressing climate change.”
Increasingly, fire-prone states like California are requiring homeowners to clear the trees and shrubs in a radius surrounding their home. This buffer zone, known as a defensible space, can dramatically reduce the risk that a wildfire will ignite a building.
People chose to live in these neighborhoods precisely because they love the vegetation, Cossel said. “I understand why people don’t want to remove them,” he said. “But we can’t live in that world anymore because of these fires.”
This story was originally published by Grist and is reproduced here as part of the Climate Desk collaboration.

title: WhatsApp Gets a Handy @all Feature for Group Chats
summary: A new software update builds on WhatsApp’s group chat chops by adding anonymous polls and introducing an easier way to start a smaller private chat away from the larger group.
full_text:
The group chat is the last truly heavyweight institution of modern life. It’s one of the most reliable means of daily communication, used for just about anything from planning to catching up.
WhatsApp is counting over 3 billion users, and it’s a fair bet most of them are in at least one group chat; the platform has supported groups of up to 1,024 members since 2022.
An update that began rolling out on August 4 follows a run of group-focused releases earlier this year, including group message history, member tags, and event reminders. Taken together, it’s a clear signal of WhatsApp’s reliance on group chats as one of its defining features.
The platform’s latest update is designed to improve its usage, and it’s rolling out gradually. Here’s everything you need to know.
@all
Typing @all allows every member of the group to be notified, even the ones who muted the chat years ago. @all is designed to punch through and override the mute settings and notification preferences you set at chat level.
WhatsApp pitches this as a tool for the urgent stuff, like updates, changes, and last-minute cancellations. It has, however, also clearly anticipated the feature’s spam potential.
The spam safeguards thus work on two levels. In groups larger than 32 people, only admins can trigger @all, and the override itself has an off switch. You can also manually mute @all alerts entirely in your notification settings, a separate control from muting the chat itself. The 32-person threshold is the same cap WhatsApp applies to group calls. It’s the platform’s rough dividing line between a chat and a broadcast channel.
Polls
WhatsApp’s polling feature has been around since 2022 and is end-to-end encrypted like everything else on the platform. It is also, though, where many a group chat goes to stall. The poll fixes in the latest update are pragmatic.
You can now set an end time that automatically locks voting when it expires, giving the group a hard deadline to vote. Interestingly, you also have the option to hide voter names. Until now, WhatsApp polls were transparent by design, and everyone could see exactly who voted for what. Anonymizing votes now also exist inside an end-to-end encrypted system, where the whole architecture is built around verifying who sent what.
And you can now also edit a poll question within 15 minutes of posting it, which is the same grace window WhatsApp gives you to edit a regular message. Revolutionary stuff for the poll fiends among us.
Create Group Chats From Existing Groups
WhatsApp is formalizing the splinter chat. You can now whip up a new group chat from an existing one in a single tap, pulling members into a smaller group chat without having to manually add them one by one. The official use cases are surprises and side conversations that would otherwise clutter the main chat.
Usernames Are Coming
Away from group chats, WhatsApp also recently announced that usernames will launch later this year, allowing people to connect without sharing their phone numbers. The optional feature is designed as an added layer of privacy: Usernames can be changed or removed at any time and do not need to match your identity on another platform.
Reservations began rolling out in June, with eligible users able to claim a new name—or transfer an existing Facebook or Instagram handle—under the Account section in Settings. Users will also be able to add on a unique four-digit key before allowing someone can contact them.
WhatsApp says names associated with celebrities, public figures, and government bodies, including convincing imitations, will be reserved for their legitimate owners. The username land grab has officially begun.
This story was originally published by WIRED Middle East.

title: Best Solar Generators for Off-Grid Trips, RVs, and Home Backup
summary: If you want to capture the sun’s power with solar panels, these are the best solar generators I’ve tested.
full_text:
It's easier and more affordable than ever to capture and channel solar energy for your home. These handy portable batteries can harness the power of the sun to give you free electricity for your campsite, RV, or home. Simply pair them with some of the best portable solar panels, and you have the means to generate your own electricity whenever the sun is out.
I’ll run through my top recommended brands with a few examples, the also-rans, what to avoid, and round things out with tips in an FAQ. Many of the best portable power stations are also great solar generators. If you want something smaller, check out the best power banks, best laptop power banks, or best MagSafe and Qi2 power banks.
Jackery Solar Generators
Rather than pinpoint specific products, I've found that it's smarter to narrow it down by brand. There are a few brands that I’ve tested extensively over the last few years, and most folks will be best served by opting for a solar generator from one of these four manufacturers. For me, that starts with Jackery.
While Jackery’s solar generators aren’t the most affordable or innovative, they have consistently hovered around the top of my testing charts when it comes to delivering the stated capacity. Having tested several solar generators up and down the Jackery range, I recommend them as easy to use, reliable, relatively quiet, and built to last. Jackery’s SolarSaga panels are also among the most efficient I have tested.
The downside is that Jackery employs the proprietary DC8020 barrel port for its panels and generators. While it is possible to find adapters online, there doesn’t seem to be an official Jackery option, and I can’t vouch for what is available. If you don’t plan on matching your generator with solar panels from Jackery, I’d go for another brand.
If you need a decently chunky backup, this Jackery solar generator boasts a 3,600-watt output (7,200-W surge) and a 3,072-watt-hour (Wh) capacity. You can charge it from solar panels at up to 1,000 watts via two proprietary DC8020 charging ports (500 watts apiece). With decent sunlight, you can fully charge it in around 11 hours with a pair of 200-watt panels. The surge works well for power hungry appliances and tools, and you could use it to power a mini fridge, lights, and recharge your small gadgets over a weekend of camping, even if the sun isn’t out. The design is nice and durable with two handles, and there are plenty of ports, but I wouldn’t want to carry it far because it weighs 60 pounds. It works well as a home backup (it can also serve as an uninterrupted power supply with a less than 20 millisecond fallover) or with an RV (it has a TT-30 port).
I recommend opting for the HomePower 3000 bundle with two 200-watt Jackery SolarSaga panels, but only if there’s a good discount on it. At the time of writing, it is $1,900. Jackery also offers various accessories for this solar generator, including a carry bag and a trolley. My test unit is badged as the Jackery Explorer 3000 v2, but it seems to be called the HomePower 3000 in the US.
If you’re going further off-grid and want something that’s both a bit more rugged and easier to carry, I recommend the Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra. It’s smaller, so the capacity is around half the 3000 above, at 1,536 Wh, but you can charge it at up to 800 watts via two DC8020 ports (400 watts apiece). It’s rated at 1,800 watts (3,600-W surge) for output and has plenty of ports. With an IP65 rating, you don’t need to worry about rain or dust, and it’s shock-proof, so it can survive an accidental drop (up to one meter). The handle is relatively comfy, so it’s easy to carry from the car to your campsite one-handed, along with other stuff (most power stations this size have two handles). It weighs just shy of 40 pounds.
If you don’t need as much power, both the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 ($799) and the Explorer 2000 v2 ($1,499) are worth a look. I tested the smaller model, and it’s ideal for keeping small gadgets charged up on a trip, has a built-in light, and sports a handy pop-up handle.
Bluetti Solar Generators
If you’re looking for innovation, Bluetti’s solar generators deliver. The company makes relatively compact power stations for the capacity, has interesting portable options, and boasts a line designed to cope with cold weather. The build quality is great, and they tend to be feature-packed.
Currently the top pick in my best portable power stations guide, the Elite 300 offers an impressive 3,014 watt-hours in a compact body with built-in handles, though it weighs in at just under 58 pounds, so you won’t want to carry it far. It can deliver 2,400 watts steadily, with 4,800-W surge. It had no issues with a UK kettle and will happily run a fridge or TV for a weekend. The XT60 solar port can take up to 1,200 watts from solar panels, enabling you to fully charge it from dead in just over four hours in perfect conditions. You can also charge it from an outlet and solar at the same time to speed things up. It has every port you’re likely to want, including TT-30, making it ideal for RVs.
You can buy the Bluetti Elite 300 with a pair of 200-W solar panels, which might be worth considering if there’s a discount on the bundle (it’s $1,699 at the time of writing, which is not bad). But Bluetti’s 200-W panels are not the most efficient I’ve tested, and I prefer the larger 350-W and 500-W portable panels.
If you don’t need this much power, the Bluetti Elite 200 V2 ($1,070) and the Bluetti Elite 100 V2 ($619) are also excellent. If you are battling cold temperatures, take a look at the Bluetti Pioneer Na ($899).
If you’re out hiking and just want power for lights and small gadgets, the Bluetti Handsfree 1 Portable Power Backpack is neat. It has a built-in 269 Wh battery with a 200-watt maximum solar input, but you can also snag it bundled with a very portable 60-watt Bluetti panel ($599). The larger Handsfree 2 Portable Power Backpack ($699) has a 512 Wh battery and comes with a 100-W panel.
Anker Solar Generators
Anker has long manufactured many of the best power banks, but it also turns out some of the best solar generators on the market. Although it offers a wide range, Anker is my pick for smaller capacity generators, where it excels with smart, practical designs that look nice and perform well.
This is such a handy little gadget for outdoorsy folks. It has a 288 Wh battery (that can deliver up to 300 watts), and most helpfully, a handy pop-up lantern that makes it ideal for hiking and camping. It can fast-charge all your devices, too, including phones, laptops, headphones, and cameras. The included XT60 port has a maximum solar input of 100 watts and can fully charge in around three or four hours. If you plan on hiking with it, consider the 60-W panel bundle ($299), as it folds down very small.
From power cuts to camping trips, I’ve used this solar generator more than any other and have tested it with a wide variety of different solar panels. title: IMF 第一副總裁：穩定幣對抗美元化，可能反而幫美元開路
summary:
IMF 第一副總裁 Dan Katz 在南非開普敦大學演講指出，各國為了降低對美元穩定幣依賴而發行的本土貨幣穩 […]

〈IMF 第一副總裁：穩定幣對抗美元化，可能反而幫美元開路〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
IMF 第一副總裁 Dan Katz 在南非開普敦大學演講指出，各國為了降低對美元穩定幣依賴而發行的本土貨幣穩定幣，可能反而加速用戶轉向美元穩定幣。
（前情提要：46億美元穩定幣交易量「淹沒南非」，央行急了：成金融系統風險，貨幣蘭特主權受挑戰）
（背景補充：花旗：比特幣不會終結美元，穩定幣普及反而鞏固美元霸主地位）
重點摘要
- IMF 第一副總裁 Dan Katz 在開普敦大學演講，直指本土貨幣穩定幣的效果可能跟發行初衷相反
- 兩種穩定幣一旦同鏈，外匯兌換變成鏈上交易，當局賴以監測資本流動的中介摩擦跟著消失
- 南非穩定幣年交易量三年內從不到 40 億蘭特衝到近 800 億蘭特，蘭特掛鉤代幣需求反而更低
本土穩定幣原本是拿來對抗美元化的工具。國際貨幣基金（IMF）第一副總裁 Dan Katz 給了一個反直覺的判斷，它可能反而替美元開路。
Dan Katz 8 月 7 日在南非開普敦大學發表演講，題目是〈穩定幣：新興市場的前景、風險與政策選擇〉。他的核心論點是，各國為了降低對美元穩定幣的依賴而發行本土貨幣穩定幣，效果可能跟預期相反。
「本土貨幣穩定幣甚至可能加速外匯穩定幣的採用。」他在演講中這樣說。
機制並不複雜。當本土穩定幣跟美元穩定幣跑在同一條區塊鏈上，兩者之間的兌換就變成一筆鏈上交易，用戶透過去中心化交易平台、流動性池或點對點交易就能完成。轉換成本被壓下來，外匯活動也跟著從傳統銀行和貨幣交易商手上流失。
這裡才是 Dan Katz 真正擔心的地方。傳統金融中介造成的摩擦，眼下正是各國當局監測與管理資本流動的政策槓桿，一旦外匯搬到鏈上，槓桿就消失了。
南非已經走完前半段
Dan Katz 拿南非當例子。當地美元穩定幣的採用目前仍然有限，但與蘭特掛鉤的本土穩定幣需求還更低。他說現在還無法得出明確結論，用戶偏好美元穩定幣的原因可能包括流動性更高、網路效應更強，以及平台與跨境接受度更廣。
不過「有限」要看跟什麼比。南非儲備銀行（SARB）去年在金融穩定評審報告中揭露，當地穩定幣年度交易量從 2022 年不到 40 億蘭特，一路跳到 2025 年接近 800 億蘭特，約 46 億美元，規模遠超比特幣。三大交易所註冊用戶衝上 780 萬，託管資產約 15 億美元。SARB 當時的判斷很直接，「這不止是投機，而是居民以數位美元替代本幣的避險行為。」
南非靠《外匯管制條例》限制資金出境，但鏈上的美元穩定幣幾秒就能轉走，等於繞過銀行的申報與審批。今年 5 月普勒託利亞高等法院還裁定，加密資產暫不受現行外匯管制約束。
換句話說，Dan Katz 警告的「外匯活動搬上鏈」，南非已經發生了一半，只是還沒加上本土穩定幣。
同套機制，花旗兩年前就講過
值得注意的是這個論點的來歷。花旗財富（Citi Wealth）2024 年底就在報告中寫過，穩定幣採用成長不會損害美元，反而可能鞏固美元長期的全球主導地位，理由是穩定幣佔加密貨幣交易量五分之四以上，其中 99% 的市值與美元掛鉤。聯準會理事 Christopher Waller 也表達過類似看法。
當時 IMF 站在對立面。IMF 近年多次警告穩定幣有取代國家主權貨幣的可能，主張各國積極推出央行數位貨幣（CBDC）來應對。
現在把類似機制講出來的，換成 IMF 自己的第一副總裁。差別在於花旗當年談的是美元受益，Dan Katz 談的是新興市場受損，而且他多推了一步，連本土穩定幣這個反制手段本身都可能幫倒忙。
要盯的是出入口
Dan Katz 認為影響因國家而異。在高度美元化的經濟體，穩定幣可能主要替代既有的美元資產；但在美元取得受限、經濟基礎較弱的國家，穩定幣可能進一步推高外幣需求。
他的政策建議是把穩定幣的入口（on-ramp）、出口（off-ramp）以及鏈上交易平台一併納入監管框架。對於央行該掌握多少資訊，他的說法是「資料收集不該等到完美的法規」。他也提到人工智慧可能加速穩定幣的採用，因為穩定幣的可程式化與結算特性，很適合代理型 AI 的世界。目前全球穩定幣市值約 3,000 億美元。
Dan Katz 自己也承認現階段還無法得出明確結論。不過南非那條曲線從 40 億蘭特走到 800 億蘭特只花了三年，而本土穩定幣要不要發、什麼時候發，多數新興市場還在忙著開會。
常見問題
什麼是本土貨幣穩定幣？
本土貨幣穩定幣是與本國法定貨幣掛鉤的穩定幣，例如與南非蘭特掛鉤的代幣。各國推動的動機通常是提供鏈上支付選項，同時降低居民轉向美元穩定幣的誘因。
為什麼本土穩定幣可能反而加速美元化？
因為本土穩定幣與美元穩定幣跑在同一條區塊鏈上時，兩者兌換變成一筆鏈上交易，透過去中心化交易平台或流動性池即可完成，轉換成本下降，外匯活動也移出銀行體系。
本文源自 IMF 第一副總裁 Dan Katz 於開普敦大學的演講，由動區動趨整理報導。

title: Robinhood 鏈迷因幣 STONKBROKER 狂漲 28%，抽美股代幣成誘因
summary:
Robinhood 鏈上的迷因幣 STONKBROKER 近一日大漲 28%，完全稀釋估值（FDV）一度衝破 […]

〈Robinhood 鏈迷因幣 STONKBROKER 狂漲 28%，抽美股代幣成誘因〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Robinhood 鏈上的迷因幣 STONKBROKER 近一日大漲 28%，完全稀釋估值（FDV）一度衝破 7,200 萬美元創新高，目前回落至約 6,790 萬美元。推力來自兩項新功能，一是孵化生態專案的發幣平台 Stonk Launcher，二是把代幣化股票包成抽卡的 Broker Box，Apple、Nvidia、SpaceX 都在獎池裡。
（前情提要：BSC 迷因幣 $GIGGLE 單日狂飆 60% 突破 50 美元！幣安 CZ 近期多次提及捐贈問題）
（背景補充：標普 500 全面上鏈！Dinari 攜手 Circle，讓美國投資人以 USDC 24 小時買賣美股）
重點摘要
- STONKBROKER 一日漲 28%，FDV 一度破 7,200 萬美元，現約 6,790 萬。
- Broker Box 把 24 家公司的代幣化股票做成抽卡，莊家抽水 10%。
- 行情站顯示的流通市值僅約 4,307 萬美元，與 FDV 差了三分之一。
迷因幣圈找到了代幣化股票的新玩法，把它做成抽卡。
Robinhood 鏈上的 STONKBROKER 近一日漲了 28%，FDV 一度突破 7,200 萬美元刷新高點。截稿前 DexScreener 顯示，代幣報價 0.02791 美元，FDV 約 6,790 萬美元，主要交易池的 24 小時交易量約 260 萬美元，各池加總約 500 萬美元，流動性約 383 萬美元。
這裡有個數字要看清楚。行情站寫的 6,858 萬是 FDV，也就是把所有代幣都算進去的估值；STONKBROKER 目前的流通市值只有約 4,307 萬美元，兩者差了三分之一。迷因幣的行情頁常把 FDV 直接標成「市值」，看的時候要分清楚是哪一個。
抽一次可能開出 Nvidia
推動這波的是兩項新上線的功能。
其一是 Stonk Launcher，一個架在 Robinhood 鏈上的發幣平台，支援固定價格、bonding curve 與自訂發行方式，發行完成後可以直接把流動性導進 Uniswap V3，還帶手續費分潤與質押金庫，用途是孵化生態內的專案。
其二是 Broker Box，由 Clutch Markets 推出的抽卡機制。獎池裡放的是 24 家公司的代幣化股票，包含 Apple、Amazon、Nvidia 與 SpaceX，玩家可以直接買，也可以花錢抽，抽中的股票代幣會直接落進錢包或封裝成憑證。
值得注意的是抽水比例。Broker Box 的莊家抽成是 10%，其中 2.5% 給創作者、2.5% 給 Clock In、5% 進協議累積。這個數字比多數線上博弈平台還高，而玩家換到的是股票代幣而不是現金。官方強調合約沒有暫停鍵、不可升級，開發方也動不了玩家資金與已鎖定的獎品。
這波更新獲得包括 Ansem 在內的 KOL 與社群關注，推動市值連創新高。。
依照官方路線圖，Stonk Exchange（vDEX）與 Covered Call 選擇權功能排在 8/29 上線，屆時整套產品線會湊齊發幣、交易、抽卡與選擇權四塊。
不過迷因幣終究是迷因幣。STONKBROKER 的流動性約 383 萬美元，相對於 6,790 萬的 FDV 並不算厚，行情走勢與新功能的話題度高度繫結，回落速度通常不會比拉昇慢。相關專案仍存在較大不確定性、價格波動大，參與前請自行評估風險。
常見問題
STONKBROKER 是什麼？
STONKBROKER 是 Robinhood 鏈上的社群型迷因幣專案，生態包含發幣平台 Stonk Launcher、代幣化股票抽卡 Broker Box，以及規劃中的去中心化交易所與 Covered Call 選擇權功能。
Broker Box 的抽卡可以抽到真的股票嗎？
抽到的是代幣化股票憑證，不是傳統券商帳戶裡的股票。獎池涵蓋 Apple、Amazon、Nvidia、SpaceX 等 24 家公司，莊家抽成 10%，本質上仍是機率型商品。

title: Cloudflare 非人類流量首度過半！執行長喊話 L1：能扛 1 億 TPS 再找我
summary:
ARK Invest 數位資產研究總監 Lorenzo Valente 說，加密社群可能錯過了本週最重要的一場 […]

〈Cloudflare 非人類流量首度過半！執行長喊話 L1：能扛 1 億 TPS 再找我〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
ARK Invest 數位資產研究總監 Lorenzo Valente 說，加密社群可能錯過了本週最重要的一場財報電話會議。Cloudflare 承載全球約 20% 的網路流量，Q2 財報揭露 AI 代理請求年增 1,700%，本季非人類流量首度超過總流量的一半，這是網路史上第一次。執行長 Matthew Prince 更早之前就開過價，他要的結算層第一天就得扛每秒 1,000 萬筆交易，而現在的 AI 代理支付一整年才跑出 1.1 億筆。
（前情提要：Cloudflare 推出「AI 代理專用錢包」！支援穩定幣微支付、自訂預算防超支）
（背景補充：Visa、Mastercard 搶進「AI 代理支付」管道，但至今交易額僅 1.36 億鎂）
重點摘要
- Cloudflare Q2 非人類流量首度過半，AI 代理請求年增 1,700%，公司承載全球約 20% 網路流量
- 執行長 Matthew Prince 稱每秒約 5 億次請求中 1% 到 10% 可收費，等於 500 萬至 5,000 萬 TPS
- 他要的門檻是第一天 1,000 萬 TPS，而 Visa 研究顯示 AI 代理一整年只跑出 1.1 億筆交易
加密社群這週的注意力都在 Cloudflare 的錢包上，但 ARK Invest 數位資產研究總監 Lorenzo Valente 認為，真正該看的是財報電話會議。他說加密圈可能錯過了本週最重要的一場法說會，重點不在產品，在管理層怎麼描述 AI 代理時代的網路基礎設施會長什麼樣。
先看數字。Cloudflare 目前承載全球約 20% 的網路流量，財報揭露 AI 代理的請求量年增 1,700%，而本季 AI 代理流量已經超過網路總流量的一半。這是網路史上第一次，非人類成為主要的流量來源。
財報本身也很漂亮。Cloudflare Q2 營收 6.961 億美元、年增 36%，全年財測從 28.05 億至 28.13 億美元上調到 28.6 億至 28.7 億美元，過去 12 個月新增 986 家年花費超過 10 萬美元的大客戶，企業客戶數年增 27% 來到 4,698 家。股價週五盤前一度漲 16.2%，報 330.51 美元。
比執行長自己的預測早了一年
這個「過半」有個容易被略過的脈絡。Matthew Prince 今年 5 月 25 日上 Bankless 節目時，說法還是 Cloudflare「預期 AI 機器人流量會在 2027 年上半年超過人類流量」。結果 Q2 財報就已經越線。
掌握全球五分之一網路流量，Cloudflare 對這件事的時間表也預估晚了大約一年。
廣告模式壞在代理不會點廣告
流量結構一變，商業模式就跟著垮。Matthew Prince 在同一場訪談把問題講得很白。
如果網路過去 30 年的商業模式是廣告和訂閱，問題是代理不會點廣告。而買一份訂閱之後，讓代理把裡面所有內容都撈走，這對確保內容創作者拿到報酬也沒有幫助。
他強調這比較不是頻寬危機，而是經濟問題。技術上網路大概吸收得了這些請求，難的是誰要付下面那層伺服器、資安、出版與基礎設施的錢。
這正是 Cloudflare 一路推 pay per crawl、x402 與穩定幣支付的原因。Matthew Prince 指出，HTTP 的 402「Payment Required」狀態碼存在很多年了，一直缺的是一條夠便宜、夠快、能處理不到一美分金額的支付軌道。他認為 Visa 那種卡片基礎設施撐不起這個模式，關鍵不是速度，是手續費結構讓微額支付根本不划算。
現實跟需求之間差了幾百萬倍
Cloudflare 的規模讓這個缺口特別刺眼。Matthew Prince 說公司每秒處理約 5 億次請求，其中大約 1% 到 10% 具備商業化潛力，換算下來是每秒 500 萬到 5,000 萬筆付費請求。
他給的門檻比這個還直接。
有人會跟我們說「天啊我們好興奮，我們能處理每秒 200 萬筆交易」，我說「很棒，做得好」。但我想第一天我就需要每秒 1,000 萬筆交易。所以如果你想建一條能支撐每秒 1 億筆交易的 Layer 1 區塊鏈，打給我們。
把這個門檻放到現實旁邊，落差才看得出來。動區 7 月底報導過 Visa 的研究，AI 代理在過去一整年處理了 1.1 億筆交易。攤到每一秒，大約是 3.5 筆。Matthew Prince 要的是第一天 1,000 萬筆，兩者差了將近 287 萬倍。
Visa 與 Mastercard 都已經搶進 AI 代理支付管道，但截至本週，兩家在這條線上的累計交易額只有 1.36 億美元。
若照每筆 0.001 美元的微支付費率、以 Matthew Prince 的 1,000 萬 TPS 門檻推算，光是基礎交易費一年就是大約 3,150 億美元的規模。
常見問題
Cloudflare 非人類流量過半代表什麼？
代表網路上超過一半的請求來自 AI 代理與機器人而非真人。Cloudflare 承載全球約 20% 網路流量，AI 代理請求年增 1,700%。由於代理不會瀏覽廣告，靠廣告與訂閱變現的模式在這種流量結構下會失效。
為什麼 Cloudflare 需要每秒 1,000 萬筆交易？
執行長 Matthew Prince 說公司每秒處理約 5 億次請求，其中 1% 到 10% 可商業化，等於每秒 500 萬到 5,000 萬筆付費請求。他要求結算層第一天就能扛 1,000 萬 TPS，並公開喊話能做到 1 億 TPS 的 L1 團隊。

title: BTCPay Server 爆重大漏洞！Foundation Lightning Node 被清空
summary:
BTCPay Server 發現正遭積極利用的關鍵漏洞，駭客已清空多個 Lightning Node。Foun […]

〈BTCPay Server 爆重大漏洞！Foundation Lightning Node 被清空〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
BTCPay Server 發現正遭積極利用的關鍵漏洞，駭客已清空多個 Lightning Node。Foundation CEO 證實自家 Node 在警告發出前就被竊空，所有通道關閉、資金被掃光。
（前情提要：災情擴大！Coldcard 錢包漏洞遭駭 1719 枚比特幣，損失估破 1.3 億美元）
（背景補充：閃電網路遭白帽連爆2次嚴重漏洞破壞，Lightning Labs發布緊急更新）
比特幣自託管支付處理器 BTCPay Server 週五發現正遭積極利用的關鍵漏洞，駭客已開始清空使用者的 Lightning Node。硬體錢包廠商 Foundation 執行長 Zach Herbert 證實，自家 Node 在官方警告發出前就被竊空，所有通道被強制關閉、資金全被掃走。
BTCPay Server 專案於美東時間 8 日 11:51 發布緊急公告：
「BTCPay Server 存在一個正被積極利用的關鍵漏洞，可能造成資金損失。若你無法立即更新，請關閉你的 BTCPay Server，直到可以更新為止，以防止未經授權的存取。」
Foundation Node 被清空，Citadel21 也遭波及
Foundation CEO Herbert 在 X 平台貼文：
「有多少 BTCPay Lightning Node 被清空了？我們的 Foundation Node 在夜間遭到駭客掏空。」
一小時後他補充說明損失範圍：
- 只有 BTCPay 用於支付處理的 Lightning Node 被盜
- 熱錢包（hot wallet）未受影響
- 所有通道被關閉，資金被掃走
比特幣評論者 hodlonaut（比特幣 Zine Citadel21 的作者）也證實了這件事：
「這是針對 BTCPayserver 使用者的持續攻擊。Citadel21 的 lightning node 剛被掃光。幸好那裡的資金不多。」
目前尚未有人統計被駭的 Node 數量或總損失金額。
被偷錢的開發者發現漏洞
BTCPay Server 創始人 Nicolas Dorier 指出，這個漏洞是被受害者「被偷後分析日誌」才發現的。他感謝 Sparrow Wallet 開發者 Craig Raw 分析出攻擊原理：
Dorier 同時表示，近期成立的 Bitcoin Red Team（由 Coldcard 漏洞事件催生的志工審計組織）的 AI 掃描也漏掉了這個漏洞：
「AI 報告沒有包含這個漏洞。但這個 bug 真的很隱蔽，我不意外簡單掃描沒發現，或者把它判為低風險。」
不是 2FA 旁路漏洞
BTCPay Server 於 8 月 4 日修復了一個 Greenfield API 的兩階段驗證旁路漏洞（FIDO2 硬鑰匙帳號在基本驗證下可繞過 2FA）。但 Dorier 明確指出，這次遭積極利用的漏洞不是這個：
「這個 bug 是 Red Team 發現的，不是這次關鍵漏洞。」
目前 BTCPay 尚未披露實際被利用的漏洞細節。核心貢獻者 Uncle Rockstar 表示：
「我們正與 Bitcoin Red Team 合作完整處理漏洞細節，將很快發布詳細技術文章。」
補完漏洞不等於安全
更新到版本 2.4.2 只是第一步。BTCPay 要求使用者完成以下動作：
- 完全重新生成 macaroons 和 macaroons.db（LND Lightning Node 的授權憑證檔案）
- 刷新所有 Lightning 後端的驗證字串
- 若曾在 BTCPay 內生成熱錢包，轉移資金並重建錢包
LND 錢包 ZEUS 的開發者 Kaloudis 說得更直白：
「不要假設升級完你就安全了。」
受害者描述的攻擊模式是通道被強制關閉、餘額被掃走，而非伺服器本身再次被入侵。這表示駭客在補丁前複製了 macaroons，即使軟體更新，舊憑證仍然有效，直到被銷毀重新放出。
比特幣基礎設施的至暗時刻
BTCPay Server 的警告發布時，正值比特幣基礎設施安全狀況最糟的時期：
- Coldcard 漏洞：2021 年的 firmware bug（弱隨機數產生器）自 7 月 30 日起已竊走約 1.14 億美元 BTC，超過 5,200 個地址受害
- Boltz 停服：8 月 3 日，跨鏈交換服務 Boltz 宣布無限期中止服務，表示「駭客迭代速度已超過我們團隊的修復能力」
- Bitcoin Red Team：由 Calle 等 16 位研究者在 27.5 小時內提交 4,962 個發現，涵蓋 390 個專案，包含 85 個嚴重與 635 個高風險漏洞

title: Woman attacked by bed bugs during Travelodge stay
summary: Hannah Stephenson says the red bites have left her feeling self-conscious and embarrassed.
full_text:
Woman attacked by bed bugs during Travelodge stay
- Published
Thirteen days after Hannah Stephenson stayed a night in a Travelodge hotel, she is still itching with red lumps over her body - a nightmare she would not wish on her "worst enemy".
The 31-year-old from Bassingbourn had been out with friends in Cambridge and decided to book a one-night stay at the hotel on Newmarket Road on 26 July to save money instead of getting a taxi home.
The next morning, she woke up to a "horrible realisation", feeling itchy with red lumps over her body and blood spots smeared on the bedding — the tell-tale signs of bed bugs, she said.
A Travelodge spokesperson said: "We are deeply sorry for Ms Stephenson's experience and how distressing an incident like this can be."
Stephenson said a lovely evening with friends had turned into a horrible morning.
"It was just a lovely wholesome time of Cambridge sightseeing and pubs, and now it is tarnished by these bedbug bites," she said.
"It wasn't until I saw the blood and the bugs that I realised what had happened."
She said it got worse, spreading to her face and causing swelling to her arms.
"It's been difficult. I've had to take a lot of antihistamines, which have made me quite drowsy. I've been waking up in the night itching," she said.
"I have felt very self-conscious. There are certain social events I haven't gone to, as I was so embarrassed at the way my arms were looking and the way my face looked."
After she was left feeling "ignored" when she initially complained to the hotel, she posted a series of pictures, external of the red bites on TikTok, which she believes prompted the hotel to get in touch.
"I don't think I would be at this point at the moment if I didn't take it to TikTok," she said.
According to the British Pest Control Association, external, during the warmer months of the year bedbugs, thrive due to being more active, feeding and mating.
It said the tell-tale signs of bedbugs include red, irritating bites and small blood smears on bed linen; and small brown insects in or around the sleeping area.
If bedbugs are found, it recommends washing everything at a high temperature before putting items in a plastic bag and deep freezing for at least three days.
Stephenson has lived across the world in Asia, Africa and South America and never experienced bedbug bites before.
She said: "I would never expect this in Cambridge of all places. I am just hoping these bites will go as soon as possible and I will look normal and get on with my life."
Stephenson has accepted £2,000 in compensation from Travelodge; however, she hopes the company will be more vigilant in the future and that people will have the courage to speak out.
A spokesperson for Travelodge said: "The safety of our customers is our priority; and we maintain stringent, expert-led measures to prevent and manage pest issues.
"In the rare instance that an issue is reported in one of our hotels, we immediately take affected and surrounding rooms out of service for inspection and treatment by independent pest control experts."

title: Messi will decide when he retires, says Argentina FA chief
summary: Retirement rumours surrounded Lionel Messi at last two World Cups, but Argentina FA chief says decision will be his.
full_text:
Messi will decide when he retires, says Argentina FA chief
Retirement rumours surrounded Lionel Messi at last two World Cups, but Argentina FA chief says decision will be his.
Especially after witnessing what Lionel Messi was still capable of at this summer’s World Cup, the president of the Argentine Football Association is not rushing the all-time great out the door.
Claudio “Chiqui” Tapia said in an interview on Argentinian TV that Messi is the only person making the decision on when to hang up his boots.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Argentina and Mexico back Infantino, deepening FIFA divide: What to know
- list 2 of 4Infantino, FIFA try to move beyond botched World Cup sell-off: What we know
- list 3 of 4UEFA’s threatened legal action against Infantino and FIFA: What we know
- list 4 of 4UEFA confirms legal letter served to FIFA after Infantino’s World Cup plan
“It’s a decision that is purely and personally his,” Tapia said. “You have to let him relax. In 2022, we didn’t know if he’d play in 2026. He said it was game by game, and I think we’ve seen a great version – if not the best – of Leo in a World Cup.
“You have to let him keep enjoying playing football and after that he’ll make the decision he feels is the right one.”
Messi, who turned 39 on June 24 – two days after scoring a brace against Austria in World Cup group-stage play – has given no indication when he might retire from international football or how much longer he intends to play for Inter Miami in the MLS.
As Tapia pointed out, the 2026 tournament was no guarantee after Messi led Argentina to the 2022 title over France in Qatar. Messi, however, played some of his best football this summer, compiling eight goals and four assists for La Albiceleste.
Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain in extra time in the World Cup final last month in the United States.
Messi became the first person to break Miroslav Klose’s career scoring record of 16 goals; French superstar Kylian Mbappe ended the tournament with 22 goals to pass Messi by one.
“It was a great World Cup from Leo,” Tapia said. “We enjoyed it a lot, and we’ve got to feel proud. I enjoyed every moment. Without a doubt, he was the standard-bearer of this group in the World Cup.
“If you analyse the World Cup he had, for me he was the best player. He was break records match after match.”
Messi would turn 43 during the 2030 World Cup to be held in Spain, Portugal and Morocco. Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay also will host one match apiece as part of the centennial celebration.
The oldest non-goalkeeper to appear in a World Cup match was Cameroonian forward Roger Milla at 42 years and 39 days old, according to FIFA.
Another all-time great, Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal, suited up this summer at age 41.
Argentina are set to play their next matches in the international window between September 21-29. No opponent has been announced for the likely two friendlies that will be played.
There has been speculation that the next home game for the Argentinians could be Messi’s last.
As Copa America champions, Argentina will defend their 2024 crown in 2028, but no host nation has yet been announced for the continental competition.

title: Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan, heads towards China
summary: Five elderly people have suffered non-life-threatening injuries, with three falling due to the wind in Japan.
full_text:
Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan, heads towards China
Five elderly people have suffered non-life-threatening injuries, with three falling due to the wind in Japan.
Typhoon Dolphin has hit Japan’s southern island of Okinawa, injuring five people and cutting power to 14,000 buildings, and is heading towards eastern China, where authorities have shut down ports, schools and tourist sites.
Okinawa Island, and Amami Island in Kagoshima prefecture, are the main areas affected in Japan.
